pr_title: [ML] Retry datafeed searches on skipped CCS clusters
pr_body:
If a remote cluster has the skip_unavailable option set and is
unavailable during a datafeed search then we should retry rather
than risk using incomplete search results. Using incomplete search
results could lead to spurious anomalies being found that do not
make sense once the remote cluster is available once again.

Fixes #83838
pr_comments: Hi @droberts195, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

issue_context.title: Datafeed should retry searches if there are skipped clusters with CCS
issue_context.body:
Currently if a datafeed obtains partial results during a search it will retry that search instead of passing incomplete input to its associated job.

A similar situation can occur with CCS, and it should be handled in the same way.  If remote clusters are skipped due to being unavailable at the time of the search then the datafeed should retry the search later instead of passing incomplete input to its job.

Skipped clusters can be determined by calling `getClusters()` on the `SearchResponse`, and then, if the result is not `null`, calling `getSkipped()` on it.

Without this functionality it is possible for jobs running in a central CCS cluster to find spurious anomalies during upgrades of remote clusters containing the input data.

The post-test assertions sometimes find unreleased search contexts.  So there must be somewhere in the datafeed code that doesn't release search contexts if a search fails.

In addition there are a couple of outstanding TODOs in this test, but I thought I'd push the code in its current form for visibility.
I think the issue is that we need to clear scroll if the search response contains skipped clusters.

I removed the `indices.contains(null)` bit because `contains(null)` called on a `List` created with `List.of` throws an NPE.  I don't think it's possible for an end user to specify `null` as a list element now that they cannot use the transport client because the X-Content parser won't accept `null` elements.  So I think the check is now redundant and just annoying for test code that wants to use `List.of`.
